result.topic_en: Euler determines the friction coefficient alpha from the observed water height at which outflow begins, then works a numerical example (100 ft vessel, 100 ft horizontal pipe) showing that friction reduces a fountain's jet height to about 69 2/3 feet.

items.quote: videamus in aliquo exemplo, quanta debilitatio in fontibus ſalientibus ob frictionem oriri debeat.
items.english: let us see in some example how great a weakening must arise in fountains because of friction.

items.quote: Verum hic ſaltus etiam ob reſiſtentiam aëris aliquantum diminuetur, ita vt fons ne quidem ad hanc altitudinem $69\frac{2}{3}$ pedum ſit aſcenſurus.
items.english: But this jet will also be somewhat diminished by air resistance, so that the fountain will not even rise to this height of 69 2/3 feet.
